title: Employment agency

paragraphs.text: Part one. You will hear a woman who works at an employment agency talking to a man about jobs he could apply for. First, you have some time to look at questions one to six.
Now listen carefully and answer questions one to six.
Good morning. How may I help you?
Good morning. We spoke on the phone last week, and I'm ringing to get more details about the job.
That's right. Thank you for sending in your CV. We've carefully looked at it, and I think we have several jobs that might suit you.
That's great.
The first one is in a magazine based in North London. They're looking for a reporter.
What sort of magazine is it?
They're called Home Solutions, which publishes articles on housing every week, and they want to find someone responsible for collecting the latest news and writing relevant articles.
What are the hours of work?

Well, you will be expected to work 40 hours a week, but there may be opportunities to do overtime during busy periods. For example, some may work more than 50 hours a week and get extra pay, but you're not required to do this.
That's reasonable. Do you know what the rates of pay are?
Yes. It says you'll get a monthly pay of 7000 pounds for the first six months, and after the probationary period, you'll be eligible for a salary of more than that, maybe 7500 pounds or more.
That's good.
So is that something that might interest you?
It is, yes. The only thing is you say they are in North London, so it would be a pretty long commute for me.
In that case, the second position might suit you better regarding location. That's a researcher for an electronic engineering company in South London.
Yes. That would be a lot closer.
Your CV shows you have relevant working experience in this field.
Yes. I worked in the office of a computer engineering company for two years. What about the working hours?
For this job, you'll have to work 45 hours a week, and the starting salary is 7200 pounds for the six-month probationary period.
That should be nice.
I can arrange for you an interview if you're interested. But before that, may I ask where you heard about us? Was it in an advert or did your friend tell you?
Neither. It was a website. Then I just got your number from the phone book.
Oh, right.
Before you hear the rest of the conversation, you have some time to look at questions seven to ten.
Now listen and answer questions seven to ten.
Apart from full-time jobs, we have some part-time work that might suit you. Here, several magazines are recruiting part-time writers. Are you interested?
What kind of writer exactly? I mean, what types of articles should I write about?
Well, the first one is to do with sports reports. For this, you're expected to write sports articles twice weekly.
Well, I love sports. I'm a football fan, but as far as writing is concerned, I'm not entirely keen on that. I think I'll rule it out.
Okay. Then how about writing something for entertainment? Does it appeal to you?

Entertainment is an exciting topic. I like reading news or articles in this category, but I'm not sure if I should write something about it. Anyway, I'll think about that. Could you give me more details?
Okay. I've got your email, and I will send the details to you later.
Thanks.
And the third one is writing reviews for soap dramas.
Oh, soap drama is my favorite. I worked as a freelance writer in this field three years ago. I think it's pretty worthwhile to give my own opinions and recommendations to the audience.
That's good. And the last one is writing articles for a business economy magazine.
I'm unfamiliar with this field, so I think it might not be easy.
Don't worry too much. Experience is not essential for this job. They've got a training session for every recruit.
That sounds not too bad.
Okay. Would you like me to send you the pamphlet so that you can learn more about it?
That will be nice.
Okay. That's it. I'll send you all the information later, and...
That is the end of part one. You now have half a minute to check your answers to part one.
